Open source · every spell tunable

clips.note: REVIEW: Static from ~2.5: frozen dummy in a finished ring. | Tested (shot 50, t1.5). Side-on and front-lit. The spike streaks in from frame right at ~0.95 and the crystal ring erupts at ~1.25. The orb stays off-frame. The title card holds this clip's first frame.

WIDER: x1.15 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 04, t2.2). Reverse angle: the shield fills the right half and the orb sits small at the left third. The volleys fly at the lens and hit at ~2.3 and ~3.3. Follow delays count from the previous cast, as in REEL_FOLLOW.

REVIEW: cam2 dollied pillar (5.36,12.93) in from the right edge at ~3.8 (its 10 deg width was missed) and the tail idled. Shorter dolly; the pillar edge stays at 41 deg. | Tested start (shot 05, t2.4). Seen from behind the caster: portal A sits in front of the orb and B lies beyond it. B opens on the camera's +x side because the camera x is positive at cast time. A slow dolly right separates the two rings. On cam2 the nearest pillar is 46 deg off-axis.

WIDER: x1.15 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Shot 06 orbited 9 deg round the dummy at the same 5.4 m, which pushes dummy 1 out of the left edge (44 deg off-axis). The blob lands ~1.6, then the pool, froth and dissolving dummy.

REVIEW: After the crash (~2.9) it is a beige mist wash. Cut on the foam. | End pose tested (shot 10, t2.3: the hero barrel). The start pose is inside the pillar ring because shot 11, from outside, was blocked; pillar (5.36,12.93) stays behind the lens. Plays at 0.6x through the swell, the plunge and the crash (~2.6-2.8), so 4.5 s on screen. Cut on the foam bore, before the water reaches the lens.
WIDER: x1.25 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 34, t1.6). Low reverse: spikes erupt toward the lens and debris flies at camera. Static.

REVIEW: The blade never read: only a dust puff at 0.8. Profile at 0.4x (shot 51): the refraction arc crosses right to left into the dummy. | Shot 41 (t1.45) with the aim swung 5 deg right, which drops dummy 1 off the left edge (44 deg). The blade is invisible by design. It reads as a dust shear line entering frame right at ~0.6, a rooster tail at the dummy ~0.8, a floor cut and refraction fringes. Low and side-backlit so the dust glows.

WIDER: x1.3 from target, both up 0.4 m (owner: too zoomed in) | Shot 19 (t2.5) moved from x 2.2 to x 0. There a pillar sat directly behind the flame; on the -z axis the far pillars sit at +-14.5 deg, so the black silhouette stands on open sunset sky. The orb is behind the lens.

WIDER: x1.25 from target, both up 0.3 m (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: The ball was on screen ~0.3 s, then 2 s of smoke column. 0.5x on flight and blast. | Tested (shot 48, t1.45). The ball enters frame right ~1.0 and the blast fills centre frame ~1.25. Cut before the smoke pall builds.

WIDER: x1.2 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: Empty frame to ~0.9, static row from ~2.5. 0.7x on the eruption. | Tested (shot 42, t2.2). High 3/4 from the caster side with the orb 82 deg off-axis. A frost line races out, then the staggered crystal row erupts at ~1.1, backlit gold through the ice.

WIDER: x1.15 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: Empty arena by ~4.0. 0.75x on the lensed disk and the collapse. | Tested (shot 31, t2.0: the lensed disk). The hole enters frame right ~1.3, drifting at 6 m/s. A pan follows it to the dummy for the collapse (~2.7-3.2) and the negative shell. The old cut had it for ~1 s at the frame edge.

WIDER: x1.25 from target, both up 0.6 m (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: The column was down by 3.3, then a puddle. 0.7x on the eruption. | Tested (shot 38, t2.0). The backlit try (shot 37) read as glass. Front-lit reverse instead: the orb dives in and the column erupts at ~1.05 with the orb small behind.
REVIEW: Static scorch circle after ~3.5. | Tested (shot 13, t2.4). Low angle up the shaft: cloud deck, sigil, molten floor.

WIDER: x1.15 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: The devils stayed small mid-frame. Push to ~55% distance on the same bearing. | Start tested (shot 21, t3.0, front-lit, a bit far). Pushes in on the same bearing to 72% distance; pillar (-5.36,-12.93) stays behind the lens. Three devils spin up and merge.
WIDER: x1.25 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 18, t2.4). The 1.3 s charge is off-frame; the fog bell drops over a frosting dummy.

WIDER: x1.45 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: Static seam after ~3.5. | Tested (shot 36, t1.8). The high angle reads the crack as a line: the lava seam unzips to the dummy, the lips heave and sparks fly.

REVIEW: The 6.4 m canopy was cropped by the top edge throughout. Aimed at dummy 2 from ~20 m, the vortex, the rain and the sigil all fit (shot 52). | Tested (shot 14, t2.4). Stays at dusk because the spell makes its own pocket of night. Wide enough that the vortex is not cropped, as it was in the old cut.

REVIEW: The jet was a thin flat sheet. Lower, it is a crest against the sky with the splash on the dummy (shot 53). | Tested (shot 40, t1.4). Side-on at jet height with the sun raking from frame right: the jet is a bright sheet from frame left into the dummy, with a splash fan. The orb is off-frame left.

WIDER: x1.15 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 39, t2.6). The profile shows the whole lob. The boulder forms over the orb (frame right), its smoke trail draws the 5.9 m arc, and it lands frame left at ~2.45.

WIDER: x1.15 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: The push carried the lens into the gas: by 4.8 a soft green wall. Static, out before it spreads to the lens. | Start tested (shot 49, t3.5, a little small). Pushes to 5.5 m on the same bearing; dummy 1 stays 65 deg off-axis. Front-lit: the blob bursts ~1.6 and the gas slumps into a pale carpet.
Tested (shot 43, t2.0). 15 deg off the tear's normal, so the jagged edge, the starry throat and the sheared sunset all read. It snaps shut with a shock before the out.
REVIEW: From 8 m it was a grey wash. At 5 m the dummy silhouette and the streaks give it scale, and it opens clear so the storm rolls in (shot 54). | Tested (shot 22, t3.0).
WIDER: x1.4 from target, both up 0.3 m (owner: too zoomed in) | Start tested (shot 33, t1.8, dusk). Pushes to 75% distance on the same bearing: a fire column on glowing ground against blue sky.

WIDER: x1.1 from target, both up 0.8 m (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 17, t3.2, dusk). The night version (shot 16) was a flat green wall. The camera sits in the pillar gap on the 135 deg diagonal.

WIDER: x1.45 from target, both up 0.3 m (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: From ~3.5 the funnel top crops and it closes on the lens. | Tested (shot 20, t2.8). A front-lit funnel touches down at (0,0,10) and walks toward the lens to its target, dummy 0, in the foreground. Cut by 5.0, while it is still ~7 m away; the old cut let it clip the camera.
Tested (shot 12, t3.0). The hinge: the cloud deck darkens the sky and rain sheets fall, then dissolve to night.

WIDER: x1.08 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: The vent was cut by the bottom edge and #7fa6ff at 1750 K stayed orange. From the south pillar gap the vent and the ~13 m top both fit, the column at 36% width (shot 56); #2a6bff at 2600 K reads ice-blue. Sign-off: caption shortened, the column glow swallowed "LIVE". | Framed from shot 32 (night): 1.4 m further back on the same diagonal and aimed 4.6 deg right. The column sits at ~34% width, clear of the panel (right 77-98%, top 4-60%), and the 9.5 m fountain plus surge stays in frame. Pillars are 48 and 68 deg off-axis. The preset must come before the cast because it resets unlisted params, and duration is read once at the cast. The eruption starts ~2.6 and the panel leaves at 9.0, the out.

REVIEW: 1.1-1.3 s of dark sky between strikes. Casts 2.2 s apart: each bolt lands ~1.1 s after its cast and has gone ~1.4 s later, so still one at a time. | Tested (shot 47: violet, 0.6 s after the cast). The bolt lands at 30-37% width and the panel area is empty sky. Casts are 2.6 s apart so each channel has cooled before the next strike: one bolt on screen at a time.

WIDER: x1.3 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: Dark empty frame until the wing enters at ~1.6. 0.7x on the stoop. | Tested (shot 28, t2.9). The bird crosses high in frame, then stoops at the dummy with wings spread.
WIDER: x1.25 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 23, t3.6). The 2.0 s gather is off-frame; start as the swarm river pours in.

WIDER: x1.15 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: The jumps last ~1 s, then 1.7 s of dark. 0.4x on the three jumps. | Tested (shot 29, t1.3). A high 3/4 shows all three dummies so each jump reads. The return stroke blooms the frame white for a few frames: that is the flash, so keep it.

WIDER: x1.4 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 44, t1.7). The sun fills centre frame in flight. The pan follows it left to the dummy for the burst, the loop arcade and the ribbons (~2.15 on).

REVIEW: The trails cross in ~1 s, then 1.2 s of idle sigil. 0.5x. | Tested (shot 45, t0.85). Side-on: eight weaving trails cross the frame from the sigil (left third, 10 m away, not dominant) to the dummy (right third).
WIDER: x1 from target, both up 1 m (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 25, t2.4). Targeting dummy 2 puts the helix on the far side of the arena; the camera stands on the pool rim.
WIDER: x1.4 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 30, t3.95). The ball crawls straight at the lens at 3.6 m/s and detonates on the dummy at ~3.7.
WIDER: x1.25 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 24, t4.2). The 2.6 s gather is off-frame; start as the ribbon enters.

WIDER: x1.15 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | REVIEW: The beam runs ~0.4-2.7: the old in missed its start and the last 2 s were idle. | Tested (shot 27, t2.2). The beam spans the frame side-on; the old shoulder angle looked down it end-on, so it vanished.

WIDER: x1.15 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested (shot 46, t2.3). The whole orb-to-dummy lattice is in frame: strike 0.8, freeze ~1.0-1.7, hold, shatter from ~2.7. Dip to black after the shatter as a breath before the finale.

WIDER: x1.1 from target (owner: too zoomed in) | Tested at the mid pose (6.5,1.2,9.0): shot 08 at t2.55 (dome, ring, white-hot core) and shot 09 at t3.9 (fireball and pulsar beam). Start and end lie on the same bearing from the star at ~0.7x and ~1.25x, so the pull-back crosses the tested frame at the bang (~2.35-2.6). Night only: at dusk it was tan soot on a tan sky (shot 07). Dip to black into the end card.
